baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: RIDGE on the baseline features plus the built-in sum of each target gene's single-gene training change.
The CRISPRi screen delta (sign-flipped) for perturbation p and gene g predicts CRISPRa delta[p,g].
Drop mean_response from the best model (EXP_0015) to test whether it still earns its place.
Drop control_mean from the best model (EXP_0037) to test whether it still earns its place.

The sign-flipped CRISPRi delta of the perturbation's target genes, when used as a gene-specific feature for those target genes (and zero for non-targets), improves predictions by capturing the direct effect on target genes.
The average absolute Pearson correlation between gene g and each target gene of p in control cells is predictive of delta.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0092).

Multiplying the sign-flipped target delta by the absolute coexpression between gene g and the target captures both activation strength and regulatory coupling, improving over their separate additive effects.
Drop target_specific_replogle_delta_e73 from the best model (EXP_0117) to test whether it still earns its place.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0132).
The square of the sign-flipped target delta (with sign preserved) captures nonlinear amplification of strong activations.

Multiplying the sign-flipped CRISPRi delta of each target by its coefficient of variation in control cells captures target-specific activation strength modulated by expression noise.
The number of gene sets (from gene_sets) that contain at least one target gene of p, normalized by total gene sets, is predictive of perturbation effect.

most_useful_features.description: Sign-flipped CRISPRi screen delta of p's target genes as a prediction of CRISPRa delta.
Per-target sign-flipped CRISPRi delta(t) * CV(control expression of t), broadcast per gene.
For each target gene t of p, multiply the sign-flipped CRISPRi screen delta of t by the absolute Pearson coexpression between gene g and t, then average over the targets of p.
Product of sign-flipped training deltas of the two target genes of a pair perturbation, broadcast to both target columns; 0 for singles.
Sum over targets of sign-flipped delta times Jaccard overlap of gene sets containing target and gene g.
Sign-flipped CRISPRi delta for target genes only, zero elsewhere.
For each target t of p, multiply sign-flipped CRISPRi delta_t by (abs Pearson correlation between t and g)^2; sum over targets.
Sum over targets t of sign-flipped CRISPRi delta_t times sign(cor(g,t))*cor(g,t)^2.
Square of the mean absolute Pearson correlation between gene g and each target gene of p.
Average Pearson correlation in control cells between gene g and the perturbation's target genes.
